title: Academia
tagline: The figure code behind the PDF deliverables — stacked simulated spectra for whole compound classes, with structures drawn alongside.
method:
A compound class is a dict of SMILES. RDKit turns each into a structure drawing and a functional-group inventory; a group-contribution estimator turns that inventory into an IR, Raman, UV or NMR line list; the shared spectroscopy core broadens those lines into a curve with the right line shape and axis convention for the technique; and the stacking layer lays the whole class out as one figure with each molecule's structure inset beside its trace. The output is a vector PDF, so it drops straight into a document at any size.

The same core also parses real instrument scans — the technique modules accept either a registry sample id or an explicit source tuple, so a simulated trace and a measured one overlay through the same call.

output.note: Everything is matplotlib, so page size, aspect and DPI are figure arguments. The stacked layout scales to any number of traces — the vertical offset and label spacing are computed from the count, not fixed.

modules.what: The layout that makes the deliverables. `stack_plot` lays a class out as offset traces with each molecule's structure image inset beside its label; `stack_overlay` does the same for a paired comparison, two traces per row.
Group-contribution prediction of IR, Raman, UV and 13C line lists from a structure. This is what makes a whole-class figure possible without a DFT job per molecule.
RDKit structure handling — drawing, functional-group SMARTS matching, and the acid/base variants used by the protonation comparisons.
The compound classes themselves, as SMILES dicts: amino acids, cannabinoids, lipids, neurotransmitters, peptides, steroids.
The Biopharmaceutics Classification System drug set, grouped into the four classes.

Technique-agnostic core: `load_xy`, `average`, `normalize01`, `broaden` (Gaussian / Lorentzian / pseudo-Voigt), `simulate`, `overlay`, and the per-technique configuration table covering FTIR, Raman, UV, XRD and NMR with their aliases.
FTIR parse, replicate averaging, normalisation, and a dual-panel broken-axis overlay with derivative-based peak finding and decluttered vertical peak labels.
Single-panel Raman; reuses the FTIR peak finder.
UV-Vis spectra — broadening TD-DFT lines in ENERGY space, which is where the line shape is physically Gaussian — plus dissolution kinetics.
Solid-state and liquid NMR loading, ppm-reversed plotting, simulation from a shift list, and GIAO shielding to chemical shift conversion.
Powder pattern loading, Q conversion for Cu K-alpha, crystalline and amorphous plotting, reflection-list overlay for polymorph identification, and simulation from a reflection list.
Step-aware DSC parsing, per-trace offsetting, and glass-transition / melt annotation.
Gaussian 16 output to line lists — IR, Raman and NMR shieldings. The primary engine, because that is what the lab's DFT data is.
The only place that knows where measured data lives. Sample and measurement indices, queries by technique, and URL resolution.

The manim spectroscopy library — the animated counterpart to all of the above. Axes, traces, molecule builders, peak callouts and the transitions between techniques. Lives at the repository root beside a worked scene and its guide, not under this engine.

objects.intro: Each script writes one directory of PDFs. Run it and you get the figures; the preview links are JPEG renders of the shipped output.

items.name: amino_acid_sim_test.py
items.what: Twenty amino acids stacked in four techniques — FTIR, Raman, UV and 1H NMR.
items.notes: The reference implementation of the format. Read this one first.

items.name: amino_acid_crystal_vs_amorphous_test.py
items.what: The same twenty as a PAIRED comparison — crystalline against amorphous, two traces per row.
items.notes: The comparison layout, and the core question of the amorphous-solid-dispersion work: what changes in a spectrum when a crystal is disordered.

items.name: cannabinoid_sim_test.py
items.what: Ten cannabinoids in four techniques, plus the neutral-against-acid pairing (the decarboxylation that turns an acid into its neutral form).
items.notes: Eight PDFs. The neutral/acid pair is the class's own natural comparison, the way crystal/amorphous is for the others.

items.name: extra_classes_sim_test.py
items.what: Four more classes at twenty compounds each, in four techniques, each with its own chemically appropriate pairing: lipids (free acid against salt), neurotransmitters (freebase against protonated), peptides (reduced against oxidised), steroids (free against ester).
items.notes: Forty-eight PDFs, and the most useful script to read if you want to add a class of your own — the pairing is a per-class choice, not a fixed axis.

items.name: bcs_sim_test.py
items.what: The Biopharmaceutics Classification System drugs, one figure set per class, all as crystalline-against-amorphous comparisons.
items.notes: Sixteen PDFs. BCS class is a solubility/permeability grouping, so this set asks whether the spectral signature of amorphisation tracks the pharmacological class.

items.name: examples.py
items.what: One runnable end-to-end demo per technique — load, simulate, overlay. Doubles as a network smoke test for the data registry.
items.notes: The quickest way to check the install works and to see each technique module's own plotting rather than the stacked layout.

items.name: example_overlay.py
items.what: The minimal simulated-over-experimental overlay, in about thirty lines.
items.notes: Start here if you only want the overlay and not the class figures.

items.name: stack_plot
items.signature: stack_plot(items, sim_for, title, xlabel, xrange, descending, outfile, image_zoom=..., ...)
items.what: Lays a compound class out as vertically offset traces with each molecule's structure inset beside its label.
items.notes: `descending` handles the axis-direction convention — FTIR and NMR run high to low, Raman and UV low to high. Getting it wrong is the most common way to produce a figure that is subtly, embarrassingly backwards.

items.name: stack_overlay
items.signature: stack_overlay(items, pair_for, title, xlabel, xrange, descending, outfile, ...)
items.what: The same layout with two traces per row for a paired comparison.
items.notes: `pair_for` returns both members, so the pairing rule is the caller's choice — crystal/amorphous, acid/salt, reduced/oxidised, whatever the class's natural axis is.

items.name: broaden
items.what: Line list to curve, in Gaussian, Lorentzian or pseudo-Voigt.
items.notes: The line shape is not cosmetic: vibrational bands are Lorentzian, electronic bands are Gaussian in ENERGY (which is why UV broadening is done in eV and mapped back to nm), and powder reflections are pseudo-Voigt.

items.name: simulate
items.what: Broaden a line list onto the technique's own grid with its own defaults.
items.notes: DFT harmonic frequencies are systematically high and need a scaling factor — about 0.967 for B3LYP/6-311++G(2d,3p), about 0.95 for wB97XD/6-31G*.

items.name: overlay
items.what: Simulated over measured, normalised and on the right axis.
items.notes: Every technique module accepts either a registry sample id or an explicit `(label, colour, sources)` tuple, which is what lets a module with no registered data still be driven.

items.name: predict.ir / raman / uv / c13
items.what: Group-contribution line lists from a structure.
items.notes: This is the trade that makes whole-class figures feasible. It is an ESTIMATOR: positions are sound and relative intensities are approximate. For a congeneric series where the substituent IS the signal, a generic estimator erases exactly what you are looking for — use explicit line lists there instead.

objects.intro: Each is a SMILES dict in `chem_data.py`, and adding one is a dict plus a call. The paired comparison is a per-class choice.

items.name: AMINO_SMILES
items.what: 20 amino acids — Gly, Ala, Ser, Pro, Val, Thr, Cys, Leu, Ile and the rest.
items.notes: Paired as crystalline against amorphous.

items.name: CANNABINOID_SMILES
items.what: 10 cannabinoids — CBG, THC, D8-THC, CBD, CBC, CBL, CBN, CBGV, CBDV, THCV.
items.notes: Paired as neutral against acid.

items.name: LIPID_SMILES
items.what: 20 fatty acids, saturated and unsaturated — C10:0 through C22:0, plus palmitoleic, oleic and the polyunsaturates.
items.notes: Paired as free acid against salt.

items.name: NEUROTRANSMITTER_SMILES
items.what: 20 neurotransmitters — dopamine, serotonin, norepinephrine, epinephrine, histamine, GABA, glutamate and others.
items.notes: Paired as freebase against protonated.

items.name: PEPTIDE_SMILES
items.what: 20 small peptides and related compounds — reduced and oxidised glutathione, cysteine and cystine, carnosine, the glycine oligomers, aspartame.
items.notes: Paired as reduced against oxidised, which is why both glutathione forms are in the set.

items.name: STEROID_SMILES
items.what: 20 steroids — cholesterol, testosterone, the estrogens, progesterone, the corticosteroids.
items.notes: Paired as free against ester.

items.name: DRUGS
items.what: The BCS drug set, grouped into the four solubility/permeability classes.
items.notes: Each class gets its own crystalline-against-amorphous figure set.

objects.intro: An older, unrelated body of work kept here because it is the animated counterpart to the same chemistry — and because the CRT drug-profile format in the [drug-scope engine](../drug-scope/) was transcribed from its vertical-profile scenes. The library itself ships at the repository root as `drug_profiles/`, with a worked scene and a guide; this directory holds the supporting data modules and build tools it does not carry. Needs manim, which nothing else here does.

items.name: spectro_lib.py
items.what: The library: axes and trace builders, molecule construction, peak callouts, and the transitions between techniques. About 2,000 lines, and the part worth reading.
items.notes: Ships at the repository root with a worked scene, a guide, pinned requirements and a verified no-LaTeX render path — read that copy. The rest of the choreography is withheld, as everywhere else here.

items.name: crystal_structures.py
items.what: Crystal lattice geometry for the structure animations.
items.notes: Data, not choreography.

items.name: morph_sequences.py
items.what: The molecule-to-molecule morph sequences — which structure becomes which, and in what order.

items.name: isoxazole_video_data.py
items.what: Geometry and line-list data for the arylidene-isoxazolone series.
items.notes: Paired with the format note in `ISOXAZOLE_MORPH_FORMAT.md`.

items.name: build_montage.py
items.what: Assembles rendered clips into a montage.

items.name: make_audio_bars.py
items.what: Precomputes audio band data for the reactive bars.
items.notes: The idea this implements was later lifted out of manim entirely — see the oscilloscope engine's spectral stack.

items.name: render_scenes.py / render_mp4.py
items.what: The render drivers.
items.notes: ⚠️ Never run two manim renders that share a media directory concurrently — they clobber each other's partial-movie and text-SVG caches and produce crashes and truncated files. Render sequentially, or give each its own media directory.

parameters_intro: Defaults live in the per-technique configuration table. These are the ones a new figure actually has to get right.

parameters.name: descending
parameters.range: TRUE for FTIR (4000→400 cm-1) and NMR (high→low ppm); FALSE for Raman, UV and XRD. This is the single easiest thing to get backwards.

parameters.name: xrange
parameters.range: FTIR 600–3600 cm-1 · Raman 300–3150 cm-1 · UV 190–310 nm · 1H NMR 0.3–8.3 ppm · 13C NMR 0–200 ppm

parameters.name: fwhm
parameters.range: FTIR and Raman ~6 cm-1 · UV ~20 nm · XRD ~0.15 deg · 13C 0.5 ppm · 1H 0.02 ppm

parameters.name: line shape
parameters.range: Lorentzian for vibrational and NMR, Gaussian for electronic, pseudo-Voigt for powder diffraction. Physically determined, not a preference.

parameters.name: image_zoom
parameters.meaning: Size of the inset structure drawings.
parameters.range: Scale it with the trace count — twenty rows needs smaller insets than ten, or the structures collide with the traces above them.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.range: Traces are normalised 0–1 before stacking, so the offset is in those units.

parameters.name: lambda (Cu K-alpha)
parameters.meaning: Wavelength for the 2-theta to Q conversion.
